question: A 27-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of recurrent episodes of headaches, palpitations, and sweating. He was adopted shortly after birth and does not know his biological parents. His pulse is 103/min and blood pressure is 160/105 mm Hg. Physical examination shows multiple soft, yellow papules on the tip of the tongue. There is a 2-cm, firm thyroid nodule. He has long and slender upper extremities, and his elbows and knees can be hyperextended. The most likely cause of this patient's condition is a mutation in which of the following genes?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Recurrent headaches, palpitations, sweating" -> "Symptoms suggest pheochromocytoma" -> "Thyroid nodule" -> "Possible medullary thyroid carcinoma" -> "Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B (MEN 2B)" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Multiple soft, yellow papules on tongue" -> "Mucosal neuromas" -> "Associated with MEN 2B" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Long and slender upper extremities" -> "Marfanoid habitus" -> "Associated with MEN 2B" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Hypertension and tachycardia" -> "Possible pheochromocytoma" -> "Part of MEN 2B syndrome" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Firm thyroid nodule" -> "Possible medullary thyroid carcinoma" -> "Common in MEN 2B" -> "RET gene mutation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Hyperextensible joints" -> "Marfanoid habitus" -> "Possible connective tissue disorder" -> "FBN1 gene mutation" -> 60%
enhanced_information: The patient's symptoms, including recurrent headaches, palpitations, sweating, and hypertension, suggest the presence of a pheochromocytoma. The firm thyroid nodule is indicative of a possible medullary thyroid carcinoma. The presence of multiple soft, yellow papules on the tongue, identified as mucosal neuromas, and the marfanoid habitus (long and slender extremities, hyperextensible joints) are characteristic of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN 2B). MEN 2B is associated with mutations in the RET gene. The retrieved evidence path confirming the presence of mucosal neuromas on the tongue supports the diagnosis of MEN 2B. Therefore, the most likely cause of this patient's condition is a mutation in the RET gene. Other options, such as FBN1, TSC2, COL5A1, and MEN1, do not align with the full spectrum of symptoms and findings presented in this case.
analysis: The patient's symptoms and physical findings are highly suggestive of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN 2B). The recurrent episodes of headaches, palpitations, and sweating, along with hypertension, are indicative of a pheochromocytoma. The firm thyroid nodule suggests a medullary thyroid carcinoma. The presence of mucosal neuromas on the tongue and a marfanoid habitus further support the diagnosis of MEN 2B. MEN 2B is known to be caused by mutations in the RET gene. Other options, such as FBN1, TSC2, COL5A1, and MEN1, do not fit the combination of symptoms and findings. FBN1 is associated with Marfan syndrome, TSC2 with tuberous sclerosis, COL5A1 with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and MEN1 with MEN type 1, none of which match the full clinical picture presented. Therefore, the most likely cause of this patient's condition is a mutation in the RET gene.
